Article (plain text of the PDF):

Hexagonal-to-Square Transition of the Three-Body Lattice Energy
in Two Dimensions at νc ≈ 3.92
Verifier-Gated Discovery Lab
Preprint, October 4, 2026
Abstract
We study the three-body lattice energy Tν (L), defined as the sum of (|x||y||x − y|)−ν
over pairs of distinct nonzero vectors of a Bravais lattice L ⊂ R2 of unit covolume. We
ask at which exponent the minimizer changes from the hexagonal to the square lattice. A
targeted search of 45 abstracts found no prior treatment of this question. The difference
f (ν) = Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal) changes sign between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94, with
f(3.9)=5.300e-03 and f(3.94)=-6.238e-03. At ν = 3.918 both lattices are local minima.
The data are obtained by cube summation with Richardson extrapolation in the cutoff.
All statements are numerical observations, not interval-arithmetic enclosures. The main
limitation is that the sign change is bracketed by only two sample points, and the absence of
intermediate (rectangular, rhombic or oblique) minima has not been established.
Keywords: three-body lattice energy, Bravais lattices, hexagonal lattice, square lattice,
phase transition, lattice sums

1

Introduction

For a Bravais lattice L of unit covolume, the three-body energy Tν (L) sums the triple product of
distances over all pairs of distinct nonzero lattice vectors. The problem is to find the minimizer
over L as a function of ν. In two dimensions we parametrize L by τ = x + iy in the fundamental
domain. The hexagonal and square lattices are the two symmetric candidates.
The open question is whether the minimizer switches from hexagonal to square at a critical
exponent νc . If it does, we also ask whether the switch is a direct change of the global minimum
or proceeds through coexistence or an intermediate phase. The available literature claims contain
no reference addressing this question. The only external evidence is a targeted search of 45
abstracts for the sign change and of 71 abstracts for the coexistence question, both conducted on
2026-10-04. Neither search found the question addressed.
Contribution. We bracket the sign change of f (ν) between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94, and we
report that at ν = 3.918 both lattices are local minima. Both results are numerical.
Summary of results.
• Observation 1 shows that f (ν) changes sign between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94.
• Observation 2 shows that at ν = 3.918 the hexagonal and the square lattice are both local
minima.

2

 The model parameters are fixed as follows:
• the covolume is 1 for all Bravais lattices;
• the cutoff is R ∈ {32, 48, 64, 96}, with summation over the cube [−R, R]d in lattice coordinates and Richardson extrapolation in R;
• νdirect = 12: for ν ≥ 12, direct summation replaces FFT convolution.
The error estimate on f is the numerical one obtained from the extrapolation. No analytic
bound on the truncation error is used.

3

Method

All reported values are numerical. They are computed by cube summation with the cutoffs
above and Richardson extrapolation in R. Local stability of a lattice is decided from the Hessian
of Tν with respect to the lattice parameter, and the types of minima on a grid of ν values are
determined by numerical minimization.
The trusted base consists of the numerical summation code and its extrapolation. Neither of
the two main results rests on exact rational arithmetic, a symbolic positivity proof or an interval
enclosure. Every statement below is therefore a numerical candidate, not a theorem. The signs
of f and the stability flags were re-evaluated by an independent verifier.
The results were produced and checked by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory. A
statement was accepted only after the verifier code had reproduced it.

4

Results

Numerical observation 1 (Sign change of the hexagonal–square difference). In two dimensions,
f (ν) = Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal) changes sign between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94. This is a
numerical statement with an error estimate. The verified values are f(3.9)=5.300e-03 and
f(3.94)=-6.238e-03.
Certificate. The verifier recomputed both values. The sign of f is positive at ν = 3.9 and
negative at ν = 3.94. Only these two points are certified; the location of the zero within the
bracket is not.
Novelty status: not found in a targeted search of 45 abstracts on 2026-10-04.
Numerical observation 2 (Coexistence of both local minima). At ν = 3.918 the hexagonal
and the square lattice are both local minima (numerical).
Certificate. At ν = 3.918 the verifier reports stable = True for the square lattice and stable
= True for the hexagonal lattice.

 5

Negative results

No attempted route is recorded as failed in the claims used here. Two limitations of the evidence
follow from the claims.
• The sign change is bracketed by only two sample points. A sign change at a different
location is excluded only at the points tested; see Appendix A.
• The verified statement at ν = 3.918 concerns the local stability of two lattices. It does not
exclude an intermediate minimum (rectangular, rhombic or oblique), and no such exclusion
is claimed here.

6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

Observation 1 places the switch of the lower-energy lattice between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94.
Observation 2 shows that both lattices are locally stable at ν = 3.918. Together, these observations
are consistent with a change of the global minimum rather than a continuous deformation, but
they do not prove it. All results are numerical and depend on the cutoff extrapolation.
Open questions:
1. Is the zero of f unique, and can it be enclosed rigorously (by interval arithmetic) so as to
give an exact νc ?
2. Is there a ν-interval with an intermediate minimum (rectangular, rhombic or oblique)
between the two phases?
3. How wide is the coexistence interval of the two local minima around ν = 3.918?
4. Is the hexagonal lattice the global minimizer below νc and the square lattice the global
minimizer above it, over the whole fundamental domain?

7

A

Agentic laboratory

The laboratory ran 2 rounds, yielding 2 verified statements and 0 negative results. Every round
was preregistered before the experiment (prereg.md). The agents and their roles are not recorded
in the claims used here.
Novelty searches were run for each result. For the sign change, the queries were “threebody energy hexagonal square lattice”, “three-body Bravais lattice sign change”, “lattice energy
comparison nu parameter” and “hexagonal quadratic lattice potential difference”, covering 45
abstracts. For coexistence, the queries were “three-body lattice energy minima”, “hexagonal
square lattice comparison”, “three-body potential optimization”, “lattice ground state three-body
energy” and “three body Bravais lattice minimization”, covering 71 abstracts.
Red-team statistics: 4 counter-checks in total, of which 0 passed, 4 did not pass and 0 were
not executable. A counter-check “did not pass” when its adversarial alternative was refuted.
3

 • A sign change near ν = 5 instead of the claimed location was refuted, since f(5.0)=-2.919e-01
and f(5.05)=-3.039e-01 are both negative.
• A wide coexistence region was refuted at ν = 3.6, where the square lattice is not stable
and the hexagonal one is stable.
• Two further counter-checks (a verifier grid search with R=(48, 64)) concerned the large-ν
minimum and the global minimum just above the transition. Both did not pass, and the
verifier output names the square lattice.
Unverified interpretations were kept out of the results. They remain hypotheses with open
status: a sign change at νc ≈ 3,91837, and a first-order-like transition without an intermediate
minimum.
